questions.q: In long format, what does each row represent?
options: One entity with all its categories spread across columns
One observation, such as one city in one month
A summary of the whole table
One column of the original table
questions.explain: Long format stores one observation per row, which is what groupby, plotting libraries and most modeling tools expect.

questions.q: Which function summarizes data into a wide grid and can resolve duplicate index and column combinations using an aggregation function?
questions.explain: pivot_table takes aggfunc (for example sum or mean) to combine duplicates. pivot cannot and raises an error instead.

questions.q: df.pivot(...) raises "ValueError: Index contains duplicate entries, cannot reshape". What is the most likely cause?
options: The DataFrame has too many columns
The same index and column combination appears more than once
questions.explain: pivot does not aggregate, so it cannot fill one cell from several rows. Use pivot_table with an aggfunc or de-duplicate first.

questions.q: A spreadsheet export has one column per month (jan, feb, mar...). Which function converts it to one row per customer per month?
questions.explain: melt stacks the month columns into a variable column and a value column, keeping identifier columns via id_vars.

questions.q: What does margins=True add to a pivot_table?
options: An All row and column containing totals
questions.explain: margins=True appends an All row and column holding the aggregate across each dimension.
